query: How do I sew on a button?

goal.title: Sew a replacement button onto a trouser waistband
goal.description: Thread a needle, draw out and cut white thread, and knot its end. Position a small white button on a gray trouser waistband, pass the needle repeatedly through the button and fabric, then work thread loops on the reverse and cut the thread.
goal.final_state: The white button is stitched onto the gray waistband; final thread trimming occurs near the video end.
procedure: Pass white thread through the needle eye.
Draw out a working length of thread and cut it from the spool.
Knot the thread end and position trousers and replacement button.
Hold the button on the waistband and make initial needle passes.
Repeat needle passes through button holes and fabric, pulling each thread loop taut.
Turn the waistband over and work small securing thread loops on its reverse.
Cut the loose thread with scissors and inspect the button.

phases.description: White thread is taken from the spool and carefully passed through the needle eye.
A length is drawn out, cut with scissors and the loose end looped and pinched repeatedly before the needle is placed on the table.
A small white button is picked up, gray trousers laid out and the button aligned at the waistband while the threaded needle is retrieved.
The waistband alternates between front and reverse views while the needle passes through the button and fabric, with long white loops pulled taut after each pass.
The waistband is turned over and small thread loops are worked around the needle beside the reverse stitch cluster, followed by repeated tensioning.
Scissors are picked up and closed beside the reverse stitches; the threaded needle is lowered just after the source fine endpoint.
